findings.detail: The required method fails at the FIRST center-status expectation immediately after presenting room placement. The room numeric helper is never reached. Four other methods pass, including the previously failing explicit room-resize workflow.

The predicate demands accessibility existence and a label substring; it does not demand visibility, hittability, room fields, rectangular-face success, or committed room persistence. The app explicitly sets accessibilityLabel(centerStatus), where centerStatus is derived from plan.outsideCount and plan.points.count. No locale mismatch is evident: the test forces English/en_US, and source supplies the matching English phrase.

The failing helper resolves a broad Any firstMatch and asks exists plus label in each predicate. The trace shows existence at132.85, Find at139.30, and debug capture at147.11 before timeout. These observed intervals support expensive query resolution or availability as an investigation target; they do not reveal the returned label or precisely instrument each internal query duration.

The passing room-resize method queries app.otherElements[roomPlacementStatus] and uses a label-only CONTAINS predicate with the same15-second timeout. Its existing source comment documents prior captured Other semantics and redundant existence snapshots. The other passing manual-room test uses the same broad combined predicate but awaits closeRoomPlacement first. Therefore broad-query failure is not deterministic, and its removal is not by itself proof of cause.

The failing precision method does not await closeRoomPlacement between open.tap and status predicate; both passing ManualRoomPlacement methods do. UI presentation and accessibility availability may consume the same initial status window. This is a plausible synchronization difference, not proof that the sheet failed to present.
